\chapter{Chapter07 — CNF Reductions}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.CNFReductions}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Literal satisfaction]
\lean{FABL.literalHolds}
\label{FABL.literalHolds}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal}
For an assignment of signs to $n$ coordinates and a literal specifying a coordinate and
a required sign, the literal holds exactly when the assignment at that coordinate equals
the required sign.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[List of literals is satisfied]
\lean{FABL.literalListHolds}
\label{FABL.literalListHolds}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.literalHolds}
For an assignment of signs to $n$ coordinates and a finite list of literals, the list
holds exactly when at least one literal in the list holds.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[All literal lists are satisfied]
\lean{FABL.literalListsHold}
\label{FABL.literalListsHold}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.literalListHolds}
For an assignment of signs to $n$ coordinates and a finite list of finite lists of
literals, every list in the outer list must contain at least one literal that holds
under the assignment.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Literal list satisfaction test]
\lean{FABL.literalListHoldsDecision}
\label{FABL.literalListHoldsDecision}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal}
For an assignment of signs to $n$ coordinates and a finite list of literals, return true
exactly when some literal in the list has its required sign at its specified coordinate;
otherwise return false.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean decision for a list of literals]
\lean{FABL.literalListHoldsDecision_eq_true}
\label{FABL.literalListHoldsDecision_eq_true}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.literalHolds, FABL.literalListHolds, FABL.literalListHoldsDecision}
\difficulty{1}
Given a sign assignment and a finite list of literals, the Boolean test that returns
true exactly when at least one listed literal holds returns true if and only if there
exists a literal in the list that holds under the assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tseitin clause chain]
\lean{FABL.tseitinClauseChain}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.tseitinClauseChain}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate}
Given a finite list of literals and a finite list of auxiliary literals, process the
first four literals whenever at least four remain and an auxiliary literal is available.
Output the clause consisting of the first two literals and that auxiliary literal, then
continue with the negation of the auxiliary literal followed by the third and fourth
original literals and the remaining literals, using the remaining auxiliaries. When
fewer than four literals remain or no auxiliary is available, output the remaining
literal list as a single clause.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Negating a literal]
\lean{FABL.literalHolds_negate_iff_not}
\label{FABL.literalHolds_negate_iff_not}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.literalHolds}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let an assignment give each of $n$ variables a sign in
$\{\pm1\}$, and let a literal specify a coordinate and its required sign. The negated
literal holds under the assignment if and only if the original literal does not hold.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Satisfaction of a Tseitin clause chain]
\lean{FABL.literalListHolds_of_tseitinClauseChain}
\label{FABL.literalListHolds_of_tseitinClauseChain}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.literalHolds, FABL.literalHolds_negate_iff_not, FABL.literalListHolds, FABL.literalListsHold, FABL.tseitinClauseChain}
\difficulty{6}
Let an assignment be a sign vector on $n$ variables, let $L$ be a finite list of
literals, and let $A$ be a finite list of auxiliary literals. If every clause in the
Tseitin clause chain formed from $L$ and $A$ contains a literal that holds under the
assignment, then $L$ itself contains a literal that holds under the assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Invariants of a Tseitin step]
\lean{FABL.tseitinStep_invariants}
\label{FABL.tseitinStep_invariants}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let the first, second, third, fourth, and auxiliary
literals be literals on $n$ coordinates. Let the remaining original literals and
remaining auxiliary literals be lists. Suppose the indices in the list beginning with
the four original literals are pairwise distinct, the indices in the auxiliary list
beginning with the auxiliary literal are pairwise distinct, and the two index sets are
disjoint. Then the list obtained by negating the auxiliary literal and following it by
the third and fourth original literals and the remaining original literals has pairwise
distinct indices; the remaining auxiliary list has pairwise distinct indices; and these
two index sets are disjoint.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct indices in a Tseitin clause chain]
\lean{FABL.tseitinClauseChain_nodupIndices}
\label{FABL.tseitinClauseChain_nodupIndices}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinStep_invariants}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let the literals and auxiliary literals be two lists
whose variable indices are each pairwise distinct and whose sets of indices are
disjoint. Then every clause in the Tseitin clause chain formed from these lists has
pairwise distinct variable indices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Filling Tseitin clause auxiliaries]
\lean{FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.literalListHoldsDecision}
Given an assignment of signs to $n$ coordinates, a list of literals, and a list of
auxiliary literals, process the first four literals whenever at least four remain and an
auxiliary is available. Set the auxiliary coordinate to the negative of its required
sign if either of the first two literals holds under the assignment, and to its required
sign otherwise; update the assignment at that coordinate, then continue with the
negation of the auxiliary literal followed by the third and fourth original literals and
the remaining literals, using the remaining auxiliaries. When this process stops, return
the current assignment.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unaffected coordinates in clause filling]
\lean{FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux_eq_of_not_mem}
\label{FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux_eq_of_not_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let two finite lists of literals on the $n$ coordinates and
an assignment of signs to those coordinates be given, and let $i$ be a coordinate that
does not occur among the indices of the auxiliary literals. Then the assignment produced
by the recursive clause-filling operation has at $i$ the same sign as the original
assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Satisfiability of a recursively filled clause chain]
\lean{FABL.tseitinClauseChain_complete}
\label{FABL.tseitinClauseChain_complete}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux, FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux_eq_of_not_mem, FABL.literalHolds, FABL.literalListHolds, FABL.literalListHoldsDecision, FABL.literalListHoldsDecision_eq_true, FABL.literalListsHold, FABL.tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinStep_invariants}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n\ge 0$. A literal on $n$ coordinates specifies an index and a required sign; an
assignment satisfies it when its value at that index is the required sign. Suppose the
indices in each of two lists of literals are pairwise distinct, the two lists use
disjoint sets of indices, and an initial assignment satisfies at least one literal in
the first list. Recursively fill the auxiliary coordinates by the stated rule: at each
step, set the auxiliary coordinate according to whether either of the first two current
literals is satisfied. The resulting assignment satisfies at least one literal in every
clause of the recursively constructed chain.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the Tseitin Clause Chain]
\lean{FABL.length_tseitinClauseChain}
\label{FABL.length_tseitinClauseChain}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.tseitinClauseChain}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $L$ and $A$ be lists of literals on $n$
coordinates. If the length of $L$ is at most the length of $A$ plus $3$, then the number
of clauses in their Tseitin clause chain is $\max(|L|-2,1)$, where $|L|$ denotes the
length of $L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Clause Width Bound]
\lean{FABL.length_le_three_of_mem_tseitinClauseChain}
\label{FABL.length_le_three_of_mem_tseitinClauseChain}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.tseitinClauseChain}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $L$ and $A$ be finite lists of literals on $n$
coordinates. If the length of $L$ is at most the length of $A$ plus $3$, then every
clause in the Tseitin clause chain formed from $L$ and $A$ has length at most $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[When a clause evaluates to negative one]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a term on the sign cube of dimension $n$, and let $x$ be an assignment. The
clause formed from $C$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$ if and only if some literal in $C$ has
its required sign at its indexed coordinate of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[When a CNF formula evaluates to negative one]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.eval}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables, and let $x$
be an assignment in the sign cube of dimension $n$. Then $\psi$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$
if and only if every clause of $\psi$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Literal coordinate extension]
\lean{FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal}
Let $n$ and $a$ be nonnegative integers, and let a literal on $n$ coordinates consist of
a coordinate and a required sign. Its lift to $n+a$ coordinates keeps the same required
sign and places the coordinate among the first $n$ coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[List of lifted literals]
\lean{FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral}
Let $n$ and $a$ be nonnegative integers, and let a DNF term on $n$ coordinates be given.
The list of its lifted literals is obtained by lifting each literal to the first $n$
coordinates of the enlarged set of $n+a$ coordinates, preserving their order.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tseitin auxiliary literals]
\lean{FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal}
Let $n$, $c$, and $b$ be natural numbers, and let $i$ be a clause index in
$	ext{Fin}(c)$. The construction assigns a list of $b$ literals on $n+bc$ coordinates,
one for each position $j$ in $	ext{Fin}(b)$. The literal at position $j$ uses coordinate
$n+jc+i$ and has required sign $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the Lifted Literal List]
\lean{FABL.length_tseitinLiftLiterals}
\label{FABL.length_tseitinLiftLiterals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers, and let $T$ be a term on $n$ coordinates whose
literals have pairwise distinct coordinates. The list obtained by lifting the literals
of $T$ to the enlarged coordinate set of size $n+a$ has length equal to the width of
$T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the Auxiliary Literal List]
\lean{FABL.length_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\label{FABL.length_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$, $c$, and $b$ be natural numbers, and choose a clause index $i$ with $0 \le i <
c$. The auxiliary literal list for that clause has length $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct lifted literal indices]
\lean{FABL.nodupIndices_tseitinLiftLiterals}
\label{FABL.nodupIndices_tseitinLiftLiterals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral, FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers, and let a DNF term on $n$ variables have pairwise
distinct literal indices. After lifting its literals to the variable set of size $n+a$,
their indices remain pairwise distinct.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct auxiliary literal indices]
\lean{FABL.nodupIndices_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\label{FABL.nodupIndices_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$, $c$, and $b$ be natural numbers, and let $j$ be a clause index in
$	ext{Fin}(c)$. The list of auxiliary literals for clause $j$, with variable coordinates
in $	ext{Fin}(n+b c)$, has pairwise distinct variable indices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Disjointness of lifted and auxiliary coordinates]
\lean{FABL.disjoint_tseitinLiftLiterals_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\label{FABL.disjoint_tseitinLiftLiterals_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral, FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$, the number of clauses $c$, and the block size $b$ be natural numbers. Let a
term on $n$ coordinates consist of a list of literals whose coordinate indices are
pairwise distinct, and choose a clause index $k\in\text{Fin}(c)$. Extend each term
literal to the first $n$ coordinates among $n+bc$ coordinates, and form the auxiliary
literals for clause $k$ on its block of $b$ coordinates. The sets of coordinate indices
in these two lists are disjoint.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Terms from the Tseitin clause chain]
\lean{FABL.tseitinClauseTerms}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.tseitinClauseTerms}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal, FABL.tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinClauseChain_nodupIndices}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let a literal on $n$ coordinates specify a coordinate
and a required sign. Given two lists of such literals, assume that the coordinates
within each list are pairwise distinct and that the two lists use disjoint coordinates.
The Tseitin clause-chain construction applied to these lists yields clauses with
pairwise distinct coordinates; regard each clause as a disjunctive-normal-form term by
taking its literals and their coordinate list.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the Tseitin Clause Terms]
\lean{FABL.length_tseitinClauseTerms}
\label{FABL.length_tseitinClauseTerms}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinClauseTerms}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $L$ and $A$ be lists of literals on $n$
coordinates. Suppose the coordinates of the literals in each list are pairwise distinct,
and the two lists use disjoint sets of coordinates. The number of terms obtained from
their Tseitin clause chain equals the number of clauses in that chain.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Width of a Tseitin clause term]
\lean{FABL.width_le_three_of_mem_tseitinClauseTerms}
\label{FABL.width_le_three_of_mem_tseitinClauseTerms}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.Literal, FABL.length_le_three_of_mem_tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinClauseTerms}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $L$ and $A$ be lists of literals on $n$
coordinates. Suppose the coordinate indices in each list are pairwise distinct, the two
lists have disjoint sets of coordinate indices, and $|L|\le |A|+3$. Every term in the
Tseitin clause terms formed from $L$ and $A$ then has width at most $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Satisfaction of generated clauses]
\lean{FABL.literalListsHold_iff_tseitinClauseTerms}
\label{FABL.literalListsHold_iff_tseitinClauseTerms}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal, FABL.literalListsHold, FABL.tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinClauseChain_nodupIndices, FABL.tseitinClauseTerms}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $L$ and $A$ be finite lists of literals on $n$
coordinates whose indices are pairwise distinct within each list and disjoint between
the lists, and let $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$ be an assignment. Every clause in the chain
constructed from $L$ using the auxiliary literals in $A$ contains a literal satisfied by
$x$ if and only if every corresponding clause term evaluates to $-1$ on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Clause at a given position]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFTerm}
For a conjunctive normal form formula with $k$ clauses and an index $i$ satisfying $0\le
i<k$, the clause at position $i$ is the $i$th clause of the formula.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership of an indexed clause]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt_mem}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.size}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula and let $i$ be a valid index among its clauses. The clause
at position $i$ belongs to the list of clauses of $\psi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Width three clause block]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitinClauseBlock}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitinClauseBlock}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.disjoint_tseitinLiftLiterals_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.nodupIndices_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.nodupIndices_tseitinLiftLiterals, FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.tseitinClauseTerms, FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a CNF formula on $n$ coordinates and a natural
number $w$ be given, and choose a clause index $i$ in the formula. The width-three
clause block is a list of DNF terms on $n+(w-3)c$ coordinates, where $c$ is the number
of clauses; it is formed from the lifted literals of clause $i$ and the auxiliary
literals assigned to that clause, using the Tseitin clause-term construction.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Auxiliary coordinate count]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitinAuxiliaryCount}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitinAuxiliaryCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size}
For a CNF formula with $c$ clauses and a natural number $w$, the auxiliary coordinate
count is $(w-3)c$, where subtraction is truncated at zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Width-three Tseitin construction]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitin}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitin}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.widthThreeTseitinClauseBlock}
Given a CNF formula on $n$ coordinates and a natural number $w$, let $c$ be the number
of clauses in the formula. The construction is a CNF formula on $n+(w-3)c$ coordinates
whose clauses are obtained by concatenating, in clause order, the width-three Tseitin
clause blocks associated with the input formula, $w$, and each clause index.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Flattened list length bound]
\lean{FABL.length_flatten_le_mul}
\label{FABL.length_flatten_le_mul}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be any type, let $L$ be a finite list of finite lists of elements of $A$, and
let $b$ be a natural number. If every list in $L$ has length at most $b$, then
flattening $L$ produces a list of length at most $b$ times the length of $L$.
\end{theorem}

Let $F$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables, let $w$ be an integer with $3\le w$ and with
every clause of $F$ containing at most $w$ literals, and choose a clause of $F$. The
width-$3$ Tseitin clause block constructed from that clause has at most $w-2$ clauses.
\end{theorem}

  {context}

\proofstep
  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_gateCoordinate}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004}
Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let $w$ be a natural number with $3\leq w$. If every clause
of $F$ has width at most $w$, then the number of clauses in its width-three Tseitin
transformation is at most $(w-2)|F|$, where $|F|$ denotes the number of clauses of $F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Auxiliary Variable Count]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitin_auxiliaryCount_eq}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitin_auxiliaryCount_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.widthThreeTseitinAuxiliaryCount}
\difficulty{1}
For a finite CNF formula $F$ with $s$ clauses and any natural-number width parameter
$w$, the auxiliary-variable count is $(w-3)s$.
\end{theorem}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p103-b002}
Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let $w$ be a natural number with $3\leq w$. If every clause
of $F$ has width at most $w$, then every clause of its width-three Tseitin
transformation has width at most $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restriction of an assignment]
\lean{FABL.restrictCNFAssignment}
\label{FABL.restrictCNFAssignment}
\leanok
Given an assignment of signs to $n+a$ coordinates, its restriction to the first $n$
coordinates is the assignment that agrees with it on each of those coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Extension of a CNF assignment]
\lean{FABL.extendCNFAssignment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{FABL.extendCNFAssignment}
\leanok
Let $n$ and $a$ be nonnegative integers. Given assignments of signs in $\{-1,1\}$ to the
first $n$ coordinates and to the $a$ auxiliary coordinates, their extension to $n+a$
coordinates agrees with the first assignment on the first block and with the auxiliary
assignment on the second block.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Extension on original coordinates]
\lean{FABL.extendCNFAssignment_castAdd}
\label{FABL.extendCNFAssignment_castAdd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.extendCNFAssignment}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ and $r$ be nonnegative integers, let $a\in\{-1,1\}^n$ be an assignment, and let
$b\in\{-1,1\}^r$ be an auxiliary assignment. In the concatenated assignment on $n+r$
coordinates, coordinate $i$ equals $a_i$ for every $i<n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Extension on auxiliary coordinates]
\lean{FABL.extendCNFAssignment_natAdd}
\label{FABL.extendCNFAssignment_natAdd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.extendCNFAssignment}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ and $r$ be nonnegative integers, let $a\in\{-1,1\}^n$ be an assignment, and let
$b\in\{-1,1\}^r$ be an auxiliary assignment. In the concatenated assignment on $n+r$
coordinates, coordinate $n+j$ equals $b_j$ for every $j<r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restriction of an extended assignment]
\lean{FABL.restrict_extendCNFAssignment}
\label{FABL.restrict_extendCNFAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.restrictCNFAssignment}
\difficulty{3}
Let an assignment give signs to $n$ original variables together with a further $m$
auxiliary variables. Extending an assignment on the original variables by any assignment
on the auxiliary variables, then restricting to the original variables, recovers the
original assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Satisfaction of the original clause]
\lean{FABL.clauseAt_true_of_widthThreeTseitinClauseBlock_true}
\label{FABL.clauseAt_true_of_widthThreeTseitinClauseBlock_true}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.disjoint_tseitinLiftLiterals_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.literalHolds, FABL.literalListHolds_of_tseitinClauseChain, FABL.literalListsHold, FABL.literalListsHold_iff_tseitinClauseTerms, FABL.nodupIndices_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.nodupIndices_tseitinLiftLiterals, FABL.restrictCNFAssignment, FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral, FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals, FABL.widthThreeTseitinClauseBlock}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $n$ sign variables, let $w$ be a natural
number, and choose a clause index $i$ of $\psi$. If an assignment to the
original variables and the $(w-3)|\psi|$ auxiliary variables makes every
clause in the width-three Tseitin block for clause $i$ true, then the original clause
$i$ is true when evaluated on the restriction of that assignment to the original
variables.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_gateCoordinate}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p019-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
Let $F$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables, let $w$ be any natural number, and let $y$ be
an assignment to the original and auxiliary variables, of total length $n+(w-3)|F|$. If
the width-three Tseitin transformation evaluates to the satisfying sign at $y$, then $F$
evaluates to the satisfying sign on the restriction of $y$ to the original variables.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indices in a Tseitin clause chain]
\lean{FABL.index_mem_original_or_auxiliary_of_mem_tseitinClauseChain}
\label{FABL.index_mem_original_or_auxiliary_of_mem_tseitinClauseChain}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.tseitinClauseChain}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let the original literals and auxiliary literals be
finite lists of literals on the $n$ coordinates. If a clause belongs to the clause chain
generated from these two lists and a literal belongs to that clause, then the literal's
coordinate index occurs among the indices of the original literals or among the indices
of the auxiliary literals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Base assignment for width-three extension]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitinBaseAssignment}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitinBaseAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.extendCNFAssignment}
Given a conjunctive normal form formula on $n$ coordinates, a natural number $w$, and an
assignment of signs to those $n$ coordinates, extend the assignment to $n+(w-3)|\mathcal
C|$ coordinates by assigning sign $+1$ to every added coordinate, where $|\mathcal C|$
is the number of clauses.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local Tseitin clause assignment]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitinLocalAssignment}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitinLocalAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux, FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals, FABL.widthThreeTseitinBaseAssignment}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables, let $w$ be a
natural number, and let $a\in\{\pm1\}^n$ be an assignment. For each clause index $i$ of
$F$, the local assignment on $n+(w-3)|F|$ variables is obtained by filling the lifted
literals of clause $i$ and its auxiliary literals into the base assignment.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tseitin auxiliary assignment]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitinProof}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitinProof}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.widthThreeTseitinLocalAssignment}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables, let $w$ be a
natural number, and let $a\in\{\pm1\}^n$ be an assignment. The assignment on the
$(w-3)|F|$ auxiliary variables is defined coordinatewise: an auxiliary coordinate
determines a clause position and a within-clause auxiliary position, and its value is
the corresponding coordinate of the local assignment for that clause.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Completed Tseitin assignment]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitinCompletedAssignment}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitinCompletedAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.widthThreeTseitinProof}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables, let $w$ be a
natural number, and let $a\in\{\pm1\}^n$ be an assignment. The completed assignment on
$n+(w-3)|F|$ variables is the extension of $a$ by the auxiliary assignment determined by
$F$, $w$, and $a$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Agreement of Completed and Local Assignments]
\lean{FABL.widthThreeTseitinCompletedAssignment_eq_local_of_mem_chain}
\label{FABL.widthThreeTseitinCompletedAssignment_eq_local_of_mem_chain}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseAt, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.Literal, FABL.disjoint_tseitinLiftLiterals_tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.extendCNFAssignment_castAdd, FABL.fillTseitinClauseAux_eq_of_not_mem, FABL.index_mem_original_or_auxiliary_of_mem_tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinAuxiliaryLiterals, FABL.tseitinClauseChain, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral, FABL.tseitinLiftLiterals, FABL.widthThreeTseitinBaseAssignment, FABL.widthThreeTseitinCompletedAssignment, FABL.widthThreeTseitinLocalAssignment, FABL.widthThreeTseitinProof}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$, a clause width parameter $w$, and a finite CNF formula on $n$ variables be
given, and let $x$ be a sign assignment to its variables. For any clause in the Tseitin
chain formed from a chosen clause of the formula and its auxiliary literals, and any
literal in that clause, the completed assignment agrees with the local assignment for
that chosen clause at the literal’s coordinate.
\end{theorem}

Let $F$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables, let $w$ be a natural-number width parameter,
and let $x$ be an assignment to the original variables. If $F$ evaluates to the
satisfying sign at $x$, then there is an assignment to $(w-3)|F|$ auxiliary variables
such that the width-three Tseitin transformation of $F$ evaluates to the satisfying sign
on the combined assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Satisfiability Equivalence for the Transformation]

Let $F$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables, let $w$ be any natural number, and let $x$ be
an assignment to its variables. The formula $F$ evaluates to the satisfying sign at $x$
if and only if there is an assignment to $(w-3)|F|$ auxiliary variables for which the
width-three Tseitin transformation evaluates to the satisfying sign on the combined
assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Term from three literals]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.ofThree}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.ofThree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $L_1,L_2,L_3$ be literals on $n$ variables whose
variable coordinates are pairwise distinct. The associated conjunction term is the
ordered list $(L_1,L_2,L_3)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Padding literal]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i\in\{0,1,2\}$, and let $s\in\{\pm1\}$. The padding
literal on $n+3$ variables has coordinate $n+i$ and requires sign $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct padding coordinates]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral_index_ne}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral_index_ne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral}
\difficulty{2}
For any two distinct coordinates among three additional variables, the corresponding
padding literals have distinct variable indices, regardless of their required signs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lifted and Padding Indices Are Distinct]
\lean{FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral_index_ne_exactlyThreePaddingLiteral}
\label{FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral_index_ne_exactlyThreePaddingLiteral}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Sign, FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $L$ be a literal on $n$ coordinates, let $i$ be one of
three padding positions, and let $r$ be a sign. After lifting $L$ to $n+3$ coordinates,
its index differs from the index of the padding literal at position $i$ with required
sign $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padding clauses to three literals]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreePadClause}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreePadClause}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.ofThree, FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral, FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral_index_ne, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral_index_ne_exactlyThreePaddingLiteral}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let a term on $n$ variables have pairwise distinct
literal indices. The construction gives a list of terms on $n+3$ variables: for a term
with no literals, it gives the eight triples of padding literals with all sign choices;
for one literal, it gives the four triples formed from its lifted literal and every sign
choice on two padding variables; for two literals, it gives the two triples formed from
their lifted literals and either sign of one padding literal; for three literals, it
gives the single triple of their lifted literals. For terms of every other length, it
gives the empty list.
\end{definition}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
Let $C$ be a clause of width at most three. Every clause in the list produced by padding
$C$ with three variables has width exactly three.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Number of padded clauses]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreePadClause_length_le_eight}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreePadClause_length_le_eight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.exactlyThreePadClause}
\difficulty{4}
For every clause, the list of clauses produced by padding it with three variables has
length at most eight.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of padded clauses]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreePadClause_eval_iff}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreePadClause_eval_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.ofThree, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.exactlyThreePadClause, FABL.exactlyThreePaddingLiteral, FABL.restrictCNFAssignment, FABL.tseitinLiftLiteral}
\difficulty{5}
Let $C$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ sign variables, with no variable index
repeated and with at most three literals. Extend an assignment to these variables by
three additional sign variables, and restrict it back to the original variables. Every
clause in the specified padding of $C$ evaluates to $-1$ under the extended assignment
if and only if $C$ evaluates to $-1$ under the restricted assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Three-literal CNF padding]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreeCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreeCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.exactlyThreePadClause}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F$ be a conjunctive normal form formula on $n$
variables. Its padded formula on $n+3$ variables has as clauses the concatenation, in
the original order, of the padded clause lists obtained from each clause of $F$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width of padded clauses]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreeCNF_clause_width_eq_three}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreeCNF_clause_width_eq_three}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr, FABL.CNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_of_mem, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.exactlyThreeCNF, FABL.exactlyThreePadClause_width_eq_three}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $F$ be a conjunctive normal form on $n$ variables whose
clauses each have width at most $3$. Every clause in the exactly-three-literal
conversion of $F$ to a formula on $n+3$ variables has width exactly $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Padding clauses to three literals]
\lean{FABL.length_bind_exactlyThreePadClause_le}
\label{FABL.length_bind_exactlyThreePadClause_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.exactlyThreePadClause, FABL.exactlyThreePadClause_length_le_eight}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite list of DNF terms on $n$ variables, replace each term by its
exactly-three-literal padding list using three new variables. The concatenated list has
length at most eight times the number of original terms.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size bound for the three-literal conversion]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreeCNF_size_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreeCNF_size_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.exactlyThreeCNF, FABL.length_bind_exactlyThreePadClause_le}
\difficulty{1}
For every conjunctive normal form $\psi$, the number of clauses in its three-literal
conversion is at most eight times the number of clauses in $\psi$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\psi$ be a conjunctive normal form on $n$ sign
variables whose width is at most $3$, and let $x$ be an assignment to those variables
together with three additional sign variables. The formula obtained by the specified
three-literal conversion evaluates to $-1$ on $x$ if and only if $\psi$ evaluates to
$-1$ on the restriction of $x$ to its original $n$ variables.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Exactly Three-Literal Tseitin Conversion]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreeTseitin}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002
}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreeTseitin}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.exactlyThreeCNF, FABL.widthThreeTseitin}
Let $n,w$ be natural numbers and let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables. Applying
the width-$w$ Tseitin conversion and then the exactly-three-literal conversion produces
a CNF formula on $n+(w-3)|\varphi|+3$ variables, where $|\varphi|$ is the number of clauses in $\varphi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width of clauses after Tseitin conversion]
\lean{FABL.exactlyThreeTseitin_clause_width_eq_three}
\label{FABL.exactlyThreeTseitin_clause_width_eq_three}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.CNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.exactlyThreeCNF_clause_width_eq_three, FABL.exactlyThreeTseitin, FABL.widthThreeTseitin, FABL.widthThreeTseitin_width_le}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\psi$ be a conjunctive normal form of width at most $w$, where $w\geq 3$. Every
clause in its three-literal Tseitin conversion has width exactly three.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
Let $\psi$ be a finite CNF formula, and let $w$ be a natural number with $3\le w$ such
that every clause of $\psi$ has width at most $w$. The exactly-three Tseitin
transformation of $\psi$ with parameter $w$ has at most $8(w-2)|\psi|$ clauses, where
$|\psi|$ denotes its number of clauses.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_inputCoordinate}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\proofstep
  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_gateCoordinate}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
Let $\psi$ be a conjunctive normal form of width at most $w$, where $w\geq 3$, and let
$x$ be an assignment to its original variables. The formula evaluates to $-1$ on $x$ if
and only if there exist assignments to the $(w-3)$ auxiliary variables allocated per
clause and to three further padding variables such that the three-literal Tseitin
conversion evaluates to $-1$ on the combined assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Term from one literal]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.ofOne}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.ofOne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $L$ be a literal on $n$ variables. The associated
conjunction term is the one-element list containing $L$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Term from two literals]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.ofTwo}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.ofTwo}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $L_1,L_2$ be literals on $n$ variables with distinct
variable coordinates. The associated conjunction term is the ordered list $(L_1,L_2)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sign associated to a Boolean value]
\lean{FABL.signOfBool}
\label{FABL.signOfBool}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
The sign associated to a Boolean value is $1$ for false and $-1$ for true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean value of a sign]
\lean{FABL.boolOfSign}
\label{FABL.boolOfSign}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a sign $s\in\{1,-1\}$, define its Boolean value to be true exactly when $s=-1$, and
false otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean and sign conversion]
\lean{FABL.boolOfSign_signOfBool}
\label{FABL.boolOfSign_signOfBool}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.boolOfSign, FABL.signOfBool}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean value $b$, converting $b$ to its associated sign and then back to a
Boolean recovers $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Input coordinate embedding]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputCoordinate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ inputs and $g$ gates. The input-coordinate
embedding sends each input position among the $n$ input positions to the corresponding
position among the first $n$ coordinates of the combined set of $n+g$ input and gate
coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gate coordinate embedding]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ inputs and $g$ gates. The gate-coordinate
embedding sends each gate position among the $g$ gates to its corresponding position
among the final $g$ coordinates of the combined set of $n+g$ input and gate coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Index of an Earlier Gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $N$ gates, and let $i$ be a gate position in $C$. For
any position $j<i$, the index of $j$ among all gates of $C$ is $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Earlier gate index value]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex_val}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex_val}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit, let $i$ be a gate index, and let $j<i$. The earlier-gate
index obtained from $j$ and $i$ has value $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct input and gate coordinates]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate_ne_inputCoordinate}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate_ne_inputCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputCoordinate}
\difficulty{3}
For a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, the coordinate assigned to any gate is
different from the coordinate assigned to any input bit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct coordinates for earlier gates]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate_ne_previousGateCoordinate}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate_ne_previousGateCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex_val}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits, let $i$ be a gate index in $C$, and
let $j$ be an index strictly earlier than $i$. Then the coordinate assigned to $i$
differs from the coordinate assigned to the gate at index $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct earlier gates have distinct coordinates]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateCoordinate_ne}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateCoordinate_ne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex_val}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, let $i$ be a gate index, and let $j,k<i$
be distinct gate indices. The coordinates assigned to the earlier gates $j$ and $k$ are
distinct.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Literal for a gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateLiteral}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateLiteral}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate, FABL.Literal, FABL.Sign}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ inputs and $g$ gates, let $i$ be a gate position,
and choose a required sign. The associated literal on the $n+g$ coordinates uses the
coordinate assigned to gate $i$ and has that required sign.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Literal for a previous gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateLiteral}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateLiteral}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex, FABL.Literal, FABL.Sign}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ inputs and $g$ gates, let $i$ be a gate position,
let $j$ index a position strictly before $i$, and choose a required sign. The associated
literal on the $n+g$ coordinates uses the coordinate assigned by the circuit's
previous-gate indexing operation for $(i,j)$ and has that required sign.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Literal for an input]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputLiteral}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputLiteral}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputCoordinate, FABL.Literal, FABL.Sign}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ inputs and $g$ gates, let $i$ be an input
position, and choose a required sign. The associated literal on the $n+g$ coordinates
uses the coordinate assigned to input $i$ and has that required sign.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gate clauses]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateClauses}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateClauses}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate_ne_inputCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate_ne_previousGateCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateLiteral, FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputLiteral, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateCoordinate_ne, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateLiteral, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.ofOne, FABL.DNFTerm.ofThree, FABL.DNFTerm.ofTwo, FABL.signOfBool}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input variables, and let $i$ be one of its gate
positions. The gate clauses at $i$ are the following list of terms on the $n$ input
variables and one variable for each gate: for an input gate, the two terms pairing the
gate variable with the input variable using opposite required signs; for a constant
gate, the single literal requiring the gate variable to have the sign associated to that
Boolean value; for a negation gate, the two terms pairing the gate variable with its
source gate using matching signs; for a conjunction gate, two terms pairing the positive
gate literal with each negative source literal, followed by a term pairing the negative
gate literal with the positive source literals (with only one source literal when both
inputs are the same gate); and for a disjunction gate, the corresponding two terms
pairing the negative gate literal with each positive source literal, followed by a term
pairing the positive gate literal with the negative source literals (again using only
one source literal when both inputs are the same gate).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gate relation]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateRelation}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateRelation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex, FABL.boolOfSign}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input variables, let $i$ be one of its gate
positions, and assign a sign in $\{ -1,1\}$ to each input and gate coordinate. The gate
relation at $i$ holds when the Boolean value represented by the sign at gate $i$ equals
the value computed by that gate: the corresponding input bit, its constant value, the
negation of its earlier source gate, the conjunction of its two earlier source gates, or
the disjunction of its two earlier source gates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Output clause]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.outputClause}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.outputClause}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateLiteral, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.ofOne}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input variables. Its output clause is the
one-literal term requiring the distinguished output gate's coordinate to have sign $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Circuit width-three CNF]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.toWidthThreeCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.toWidthThreeCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateClauses, FABL.BooleanCircuit.outputClause, FABL.CNFFormula}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input variables. The width-three CNF associated to
$C$ consists of the concatenation of the gate-clause lists for all gates, followed by
the output clause; it is a formula on the $n$ input variables and one variable for each
gate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length of gate clauses]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateClauses_length_le_three}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateClauses_length_le_three}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateClauses}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits and every gate of the circuit, the list of
clauses associated with that gate has length at most three.
\end{theorem}

\leanok

\begin{theorem}[Size bound for the width-three-CNF encoding]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.toWidthThreeCNF_size_le}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.toWidthThreeCNF_size_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateClauses, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateClauses_length_le_three, FABL.BooleanCircuit.toWidthThreeCNF, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.length_flatten_le_mul}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits
and $g$ gates. The number of clauses in its width-three CNF encoding is at most $3g+1$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits.
The maximum number of literals in any clause of its width-three CNF encoding is at most
$3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Circuit evaluation assignment]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate, FABL.extendCNFAssignment, FABL.signOfBool}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input variables, and let $x$ be a Boolean assignment
to its inputs. The associated sign assignment on the input and gate coordinates gives
each input and gate the sign corresponding to its Boolean value, with false represented
by $1$ and true by $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Input coordinate of the CNF assignment]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_inputCoordinate}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_inputCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment, FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputCoordinate, FABL.signOfBool}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, let $x$ be an input assignment, and let
$i$ be an input position. The extended sign assignment associated with $x$, evaluated at
the coordinate for input $i$, is the sign corresponding to the input bit $x(i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gate coordinate of the CNF assignment]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_gateCoordinate}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_gateCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate, FABL.signOfBool}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, let $x$ be an input assignment, and let
$i$ be a gate of $C$. The extended sign assignment associated with $x$, evaluated at the
coordinate for gate $i$, is the sign corresponding to the Boolean value of gate $i$ on
input $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of an input gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_input}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_input}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs, let $x$ be an input, and let $i$ be a gate.
If gate $i$ reads input position $j$, then its value on $x$ is $x(j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a constant gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_const}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_const}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs, let $x$ be an input, and let $i$ be a gate.
If gate $i$ is the constant Boolean value $b$, then its value on $x$ is $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a negation gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_neg}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_neg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs, let $x$ be an input, and let $i$ be a gate
with earlier gate $j$. If gate $i$ negates gate $j$, then its value on $x$ is the
Boolean negation of the value of $j$ on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a conjunction gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_and}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_and}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs, let $x$ be an input, and let $i$ be a gate
with earlier gates $j$ and $k$. If gate $i$ is the conjunction of gates $j$ and $k$,
then its value on $x$ is the conjunction of their values on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a disjunction gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_or}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_or}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, let $i$ be one of its gates, and let
$a,b<i$ be earlier gate indices. If gate $i$ is the disjunction of gates $a$ and $b$,
then for every input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, its value is the disjunction of the values at
those two earlier gates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gate relations for evaluated assignments]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateRelation_cnfAssignment}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateRelation_cnfAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment, FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_gateCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_inputCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_and, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_const, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_input, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_neg, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_or, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateRelation, FABL.boolOfSign_signOfBool}
\difficulty{5}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. Form a sign
assignment to all input and gate coordinates by encoding each input bit and each gate's
evaluated value as a sign, with false encoded by $1$ and true by $-1$. At every gate,
the Boolean value encoded at its coordinate agrees with the operation specified by that
gate, applied to the encoded values of its input bit or earlier gates.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.cnfAssignment_gateCoordinate}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, and assign signs from $\{-1,1\}$ to its
$n$ input coordinates and one coordinate for each gate. If this assignment satisfies the
circuit's width-three CNF encoding, then the sign at the coordinate for the output gate
is $-1$, so it represents Boolean true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gate values determined by gate relations]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateValue_eq_evalGate}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateValue_eq_evalGate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_and, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_const, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_input, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_neg, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate_eq_or, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateRelation, FABL.BooleanCircuit.inputCoordinate, FABL.BooleanCircuit.previousGateIndex, FABL.boolOfSign}
\difficulty{6}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, and assign a sign in $\{-1,1\}$ to every
input and gate coordinate. Suppose that at every gate its sign, interpreted as a Boolean
value with $-1$ representing true, satisfies the relation prescribed by that gate and
the signs of its input or earlier gates. Then at each gate, the Boolean value
represented by its sign equals the value obtained by evaluating the circuit gate using
the Boolean values represented by the input-coordinate signs.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits and
$g$ gates, and let $x$ be an input accepted by $C$. Then the width-three CNF encoding of
$C$ is satisfied by the sign assignment on the $n+g$ coordinates obtained from $x$ and
the values of all gates of $C$ on $x$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.gateValue_eq_evalGate}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, and let an assignment of signs be given
to the $n$ input coordinates and the gate coordinates. If this assignment satisfies the
width-three CNF associated with $C$, then $C$ accepts the input whose bits are obtained
by interpreting its input-coordinate signs as Boolean values.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Width-three-CNF evaluation criterion]

  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.toWidthThreeCNF_complete}
  {direct}

\proofstep
  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.acceptedProperty_of_toWidthThreeCNF_eval}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits and
$g$ gates, and let $x$ be an input assignment. The circuit accepts $x$ if and only if
there is a choice of signs for its $g$ gate coordinates such that the width-three CNF
encoding is satisfied by the combined assignment consisting of the input signs
corresponding to $x$ and those gate signs.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.acceptedProperty_of_toWidthThreeCNF_eval}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits
and $g$ gates. The circuit accepts some input if and only if its associated width-three
CNF formula has a satisfying assignment of signs on the $n+g$ input and gate
coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Exactly-three CNF padding]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.toExactlyThreeCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004
}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.toExactlyThreeCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.toWidthThreeCNF, FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.exactlyThreeCNF}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input variables. Apply the exactly-three padding
construction to its width-three CNF to obtain a CNF formula on $n+C$'s gate count plus
three variables.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.BooleanCircuit.toExactlyThreeCNF}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits
and $g$ gates. The number of clauses in its exactly-three-CNF encoding is at most
$8(3g+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit satisfiability and exact three-CNF]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.satisfiable_iff_toExactlyThreeCNF_satisfiable}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004
}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.satisfiable_iff_toExactlyThreeCNF_satisfiable}
\leanok

Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits, and let $g$ be its number of gates.
The circuit has an input assignment on which its output is true if and only if its
associated exact-three-CNF formula has a satisfying sign assignment on $n+g+3$
coordinates (that is, an assignment for which the formula evaluates to $-1$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Satisfiability of a CNF formula]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.Satisfiable}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.Satisfiable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.eval}
A conjunctive normal form formula on $n$ variables is satisfiable if there exists an
assignment of signs to the variables for which the formula evaluates to $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Encoded Boolean circuit]
\lean{FABL.EncodedBooleanCircuit}
\label{FABL.EncodedBooleanCircuit}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit}
An encoded Boolean circuit is a pair consisting of a natural number $n$ and a Boolean
circuit on $n$ input variables.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Encoded three-CNF formula]
\lean{FABL.EncodedThreeCNF}
\label{FABL.EncodedThreeCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula}
An encoded three-CNF formula is a pair consisting of a natural number $n$ and a CNF
formula on $n$ variables.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Circuit-to-three-CNF encoding]
\lean{FABL.circuitToThreeCNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.circuitToThreeCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit.toExactlyThreeCNF, FABL.EncodedBooleanCircuit, FABL.EncodedThreeCNF}
An encoded Boolean circuit is a pair consisting of a natural number $n$ and a Boolean
circuit on $n$ inputs. The circuit-to-three-CNF map sends this pair to the encoded
exactly-three CNF formula obtained by padding the circuit's width-three CNF; the
resulting formula has $n$ plus the circuit's gate count plus three variables.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Language of satisfiable encoded circuits]
\lean{FABL.encodedCircuitSatLanguage}
\label{FABL.encodedCircuitSatLanguage}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.BooleanCircuit.Satisfiable, FABL.EncodedBooleanCircuit}
Let an encoding of Boolean circuits assign binary strings to circuits and decode binary
strings, with decoding after encoding recovering the original circuit and every
successfully decoded string being the canonical encoding of its decoded circuit. The
language consists of exactly those binary strings that decode to a circuit having a
satisfying input; malformed strings are excluded.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Encoded three-CNF satisfiability language]
\lean{FABL.encodedThreeCNFSatLanguage}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004
}
\label{FABL.encodedThreeCNFSatLanguage}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.CNFFormula.Satisfiable, FABL.EncodedThreeCNF}
Let an encoding assign canonical binary strings to encoded three-CNF formulas and decode
binary strings, with failure indicated by no decoded formula. The language consists of
precisely those binary strings that decode to an encoded three-CNF formula whose CNF
formula is satisfiable; strings that fail to decode are excluded.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Circuit-to-three-CNF encoding adapter]
\lean{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.EncodedBooleanCircuit, FABL.EncodedThreeCNF, FABL.PolytimeMap, FABL.circuitToThreeCNF}
Given canonical binary encodings of Boolean circuits and three-CNF formulas, an adapter
consists of a polynomial-time map on binary strings such that every encoded circuit is
mapped to the encoding of its circuit-to-three-CNF conversion, and every string that
fails to decode as a circuit is mapped to a string that fails to decode as a three-CNF
formula.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit satisfiability reduces to three-CNF satisfiability]
\lean{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.karpReducible}

Let binary encodings be given for Boolean circuits and three-CNF formulas, and suppose
there is a certified polynomial-time map on binary strings that sends every canonical
circuit encoding to the canonical encoding of its associated three-CNF formula and sends
every malformed circuit encoding to a malformed formula encoding. Then the language of
encodings of satisfiable circuits is Karp reducible to the language of encodings of
satisfiable three-CNF formulas.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Circuit satisfiability promise problem]
\lean{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.circuitSatPromise}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p188-b003}
\label{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.circuitSatPromise}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.BinaryPromiseProblem, FABL.BooleanCircuit.Satisfiable, FABL.EncodedBooleanCircuit, FABL.encodedCircuitSatLanguage}
For a canonical binary encoding of Boolean circuits, define a binary promise problem
whose yes-instances are exactly the strings encoding satisfiable circuits and whose
no-instances are exactly the strings that decode to an unsatisfiable circuit. Strings
that do not decode as circuits belong to neither set.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Three-CNF satisfiability promise problem]
\lean{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.threeCNFSatPromise}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b004}
\label{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.threeCNFSatPromise}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.BinaryPromiseProblem, FABL.CNFFormula.Satisfiable, FABL.EncodedThreeCNF, FABL.encodedThreeCNFSatLanguage}
For a canonical binary encoding of three-CNF formulas, define a binary promise problem
whose yes-instances are exactly the strings encoding satisfiable formulas and whose
no-instances are exactly the strings that decode to an unsatisfiable formula. Strings
that do not decode as formulas belong to neither set.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Promise reduction to three-CNF satisfiability]
\lean{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.promiseKarpReducible}
\label{FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.promiseKarpReducible}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.BooleanCircuit.Satisfiable, FABL.BooleanCircuit.satisfiable_iff_toExactlyThreeCNF_satisfiable, FABL.CNFFormula.Satisfiable, FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter, FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.circuitSatPromise, FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.threeCNFSatPromise, FABL.EncodedBooleanCircuit, FABL.EncodedThreeCNF, FABL.PromiseKarpReducible, FABL.circuitToThreeCNF}

Let binary encodings be given for Boolean circuits and three-CNF formulas, and suppose
there is a certified polynomial-time map on binary strings that sends every canonical
circuit encoding to the canonical encoding of its associated three-CNF formula and sends
every malformed circuit encoding to a malformed formula encoding. Then the promise
problem whose yes instances are encodings of satisfiable circuits and whose no instances
are encodings of unsatisfiable circuits is polynomial-time Karp reducible to the
corresponding promise problem for three-CNF satisfiability.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Encoded Max-Three-SAT model]
\lean{FABL.EncodedMaxThreeSatModel}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p184-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p186-b001
}
\label{FABL.EncodedMaxThreeSatModel}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.CNFFormula.Satisfiable, FABL.EncodedMaximizationProblem, FABL.EncodedThreeCNF}
Given a canonical binary encoding of three-CNF formulas, an encoded maximization problem
is a model for Max-Three-SAT if every encoded formula is an instance, its optimum on
each such encoding is at most $1$, and that optimum equals $1$ if and only if the
formula is satisfiable.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Distinguishing Three-CNF Satisfiability]
\lean{FABL.EncodedMaxThreeSatModel.distinguishesThreeCNFSat}
\label{FABL.EncodedMaxThreeSatModel.distinguishesThreeCNFSat}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.CNFFormula.Satisfiable, FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.threeCNFSatPromise, FABL.EncodedMaxThreeSatModel, FABL.EncodedThreeCNF, FABL.PolytimeMap, FABL.PolytimeMap.DistinguishesPromise, FABL.PolytimeMap.IsThresholdApproximation, FABL.PolytimeMap.ValueThresholdTest}
\difficulty{5}
Let a binary encoding of three-CNF formulas and an encoded maximization model be given.
Suppose every canonical formula encoding is a valid instance, its optimum is at most
$1$, and its optimum is $1$ exactly when the formula is satisfiable. If a
polynomial-time algorithm returns a feasible solution on every valid instance and has
value at least $1$ whenever the optimum is at least $1$, then any polynomial-time
threshold test whose output is the one-bit indicator of whether the algorithm's value is
at least $1$ distinguishes satisfiable from unsatisfiable formulas: it outputs true on
every encoded satisfiable formula and false on every encoded unsatisfiable formula.
\end{theorem}

\uses{FABL.BinaryEncoding, FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter, FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.circuitSatPromise, FABL.CircuitThreeCNFPolytimeAdapter.promiseKarpReducible, FABL.EncodedBooleanCircuit, FABL.EncodedMaxThreeSatModel, FABL.EncodedMaxThreeSatModel.distinguishesThreeCNFSat, FABL.EncodedThreeCNF, FABL.HasPolytimeDistinguisher, FABL.PolytimeMap, FABL.PolytimeMap.IsThresholdApproximation, FABL.PolytimeMap.ValueThresholdTest, FABL.PromiseKarpReducible.hasPolytimeDistinguisher}

Let binary encodings of Boolean circuits and three-CNF formulas be given, together with

Let an encoded maximization problem for these formulas have every canonical formula
encoding as a valid instance, optimum at most $1$, and optimum equal to $1$ exactly when
the formula is satisfiable. Suppose a polynomial-time algorithm always returns a
